context.question: Is context shared between agents?
context.answer: Yes. Rules, attached knowledge, and dialog history stay on the agent. When multiple agents collaborate, context flows as needed instead of restarting from zero every task.

output.question: Can I bring my own models or local runtime?
output.answer: Yes. BYOK, custom provider URLs, and CLI agents bound to local machines are supported. Pick models by task cost and performance.

entry.question: Can one task run multiple agents?
entry.answer: Yes. One task can go to several agents. They can work in parallel and review each other before results come back to you.

orchestration.question: Is orchestration fixed to one pattern?
orchestration.answer: No. Coding delivery, parallel brainstorm, and consensus deliberation are examples. You can use public orchestrator agents, build your own, or ask AI to design a team for the current task.

orchestration.title: More than one way to work together
orchestration.desc: Split a task across agents, send one question to several models at once, or let them deliberate until a conclusion is clear.
orchestration.footnote: These are common patterns—not the only ones. AI can design a team shape for your task too.

quickStartGuide.title: Quick Start Guide
quickStartGuide.description: Tell nolo one goal. Multiple AI agents split the work, execute it, and hand back a result you can verify.
quickStartGuide.setupItem1: Open a new chat and describe a complete goal in one sentence, e.g. "Compare three laptops and draft the purchase summary".
quickStartGuide.setupItem2: Include what "done" looks like: the format you want, the constraints, and the deadline if it matters.
quickStartGuide.setupItem3: A concrete, multi-part goal works better than a vague one — the agents need something to divide.
quickStartGuide.shortcutsTitle: 2. Watch multiple AI agents split and run the work
quickStartGuide.shortcutsItem1: Nolo breaks your goal into subtasks and assigns them to specialized agents automatically.
quickStartGuide.shortcutsItem2: You can watch each agent's progress in the same conversation — research, writing, and checks run in parallel.
quickStartGuide.shortcutsItem3: Jump in anytime to correct a direction or add context; the agents adapt without starting over.
quickStartGuide.nextStepsItem1: When the run finishes, check the delivered result against the goal you stated in step 1.
quickStartGuide.nextStepsItem2: Not quite right? Reply with what to fix — the agents iterate on the same context.
quickStartGuide.nextStepsItem3: Once it looks good, the result stays in your workspace as a page you can edit, share, or build on.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Welcome to Nolo (hereinafter referred to as "we" or "our"). We take your privacy and data security very seriously. This Privacy Policy outlines how we handle and protect your personal information.

section1.title: 1. Information We Collect
section1.desc: We collect minimal information necessary to deliver our services, including:
section1.device: Account & Profile: Email address, username, and authentication identifiers.
section1.location: Transaction Records: Point purchase amounts, order IDs, and payment status (we never collect or store sensitive payment details such as card numbers or CVV).
section1.network: Technical & Log Data: IP address, browser type, and system logs necessary for security and abuse prevention.

section2.title: 2. Use of Information
section2.desc: We process your information for the following legitimate purposes:
section2.core: Providing and maintaining our digital AI computing and multi-agent workspace services.
section2.map: Processing points recharge orders and fulfilling accounting obligations.
section2.analysis: Ensuring platform stability, security, and preventing malicious activity.
section2.attribution: Ad attribution: when you arrive via an ad or campaign link, we store a first-party cookie (nolo_attr, 30 days) containing the campaign parameters and click ID from that link, the landing page, the referring site and the time, so we can tell which channel brought you when you sign up. We load no third-party tracking pixels and do not sell this data. Page-view statistics on our public pages are provided by Cloudflare Web Analytics (static.cloudflareinsights.com), the only third-party script we load there: it reports aggregated page views without cross-site tracking cookies.

section3.title: 3. Information Sharing & Third Parties
section3.desc: We strictly do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information. Data is only shared in the following required contexts:
section3.thirdParty: Payment Processing: Payments are securely handled by Waffo Pancake in full compliance with PCI-DSS standards.
section3.legal: Legal Compliance: Disclosure required by law, regulation, or mandatory legal process.

section4.title: 4. Data Security
section4.desc: All network traffic is encrypted via HTTPS/TLS. We implement industry-standard organizational and technical safeguards to protect your personal data.

section5.title: 5. User Rights
section5.desc: You retain full rights to access, export, rectify, or request the deletion of your account and personal data at any time by contacting us.

browserExtension.title: 6. Browser Extension (Nolo Browser Connector)

items.question: How is this different from giving an AI skills or MCP tools?
items.answer: Those add abilities to one agent. Nolo runs a team: who does the work, whose subscription pays for it, which computer it runs on, who picks it up next, and who reviews it.

items.question: Can I use my own subscriptions?
items.answer: Yes. Your subscriptions, your own API keys (BYOK) and local models all work.

items.question: Where do the agents run?
items.answer: On a computer or server you have connected. It needs to be switched on and running nolo connect. If an agent uses a subscription you signed into on that machine, the sign-in there has to still be valid.

items.question: Where do my conversations and data live?
items.answer: When agents run on your own computers, files and commands stay on those machines. The client is open source, so you can read exactly what it does and what it sends.

items.title: Agents can finish real work
